claim: P91 BASELINE: first measured python-xlsx compatibility water level over the 846-file real-world xlsx corpus. Not a gate — this profile records where xlsx starts, so later runs can only be compared against a locked number.

known_blockers.symptom: IndexError: list index out of range at xlsx/oxml/shared_strings.py:16 (_si_text(self.si_lst[index])) on reopen after an active edit.
known_blockers.root_cause: Setting a string cell on a workbook that has no xl/sharedStrings.xml part writes t="s" with an index into an in-memory SST that is never serialized. Saved package still has no sst part and no Content_Types override.
known_blockers.impact: Silent data loss; Excel treats the result as needing repair.

known_blockers.root_cause: Chartsheet parts are routed through the worksheet element class, which assumes a sheetData child.
<c> without @r is legal (position implied by document order) but the oxml layer treats @r as required.
Legacy OLE2 .xls content with an .xlsx extension. Documented substrate boundary, not a defect.

next_gate: P92 requires active_roundtrip_pass_rate >= 99.0 with xlsx-sst-part-not-materialized closed and a regression test that opens an sst-less workbook, writes a string cell, saves, and reopens.
notes: Measured on the standalone compat-test fork before it was folded back into ooxml-test-framework/tools/compat-test. The tracked harness additionally classifies preserve-compatible vs preserve-exact, so a re-run under P92 will report a preserve figure that is not directly comparable to preserve_all_pass here.
